name: Framepill

lead: The framepill is a looksmaxxing framework holding that how wide and well-built your skeleton is, meaning shoulders, clavicles and overall bone structure, determines how much muscle and presence you can carry and so how attractive your body looks. Believers say a strong frame can compensate for a weaker face.

It is discussed as a counterpart to height and face-focused pills. Followers use it to explain why two men with similar training look so different, and to decide where to put effort: shoulder and upper-back width, posture, and body proportions. It is a community concept rather than a studied construct, though research on shoulder-to-waist ratio and male attractiveness exists in the wider literature.

paras: In practice, followers train for shoulder and back width (lateral raises are cited), try to build muscle on the frame they have and compare skeletal width and proportions in photo threads. Some posts mention growth-focused hormone use during height efforts, which carries its own medical considerations.

The belief itself carries no physical risk. Forum threads sometimes link it with fatalistic reading of bone structure or with hormone use at young ages, which clinicians generally advise only under medical supervision.

angle.text: Followers say frame width is the base on which muscle looks good, so they emphasise width-building lifts and proportions. In their framing, bones set the ceiling and training fills it.

lead: The framepill, or frame pill, is a concept in looksmaxxing communities holding that skeletal frame is a main determinant of physical attractiveness. In this view, bone width, particularly across the shoulders and clavicles, sets how much muscle a person can carry and how imposing the body looks.[1]

One looksmax.org thread argues that the key question is whether a person's bones can support the muscle added and whether the bone structure allows getting wider, saying a good frame can make up for a lacking face while a poor frame requires a model-tier face to offset.[1] Another poster in the same thread argues that proportions create appeal when the face is not doing all the work.[1]

The term appears in titles of physique and height posts, such as a 16-year-old asking for a physique rating during a height-focused regimen and a post praising a streamer's frame and height.[2][3] Followers use it to choose training emphasis and to explain differences in how bodies look.

paras: Proponents describe frame as bone width and structure rather than muscle. One widely repeated thread says it is not about shoulder-to-waist ratio nor clavicle lengthening but about whether bones can support added muscle.[1] The same thread says the gym does not widen the frame and that rounded clavicles can lead shoulders to expand in a narrower shape.[1]
A meme referenced there compares two X-ray skeletons of differing frame size.[1]

The term is paired with height in posts, such as one praising a public figure's height and frame and noting the poster would use lifts to appear taller.[3] Rating threads attach the label to physiques.[2] Some participants reply that natural training should be tried before other approaches.[2]

lore.intro: The framepill is argued in looksmax.org threads as an explanation for physique differences between similarly trained men.[1]
